# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 2 went badly for the predictions. The naive "same as last round" guess was closer than my prediction in 4 of 5 rows. So round 3 moves a number only where a failure ID explains the cause, and it moves that number only a little.

I filled in three missing details with defaults:
- I assume the round 2 ticket set has 40 tickets (T01 to T40). Before saving the plan, I will check this against `spe/spec/spec.md` and correct it if it is wrong.
- The verdict rule stays the same as round 2. A row is a hit when the measured value is within ±0.01 for accuracy, or within ±$0.0005 for cost.
- The round 2 log has no priority or cost baseline for A, B, or D. Those cells are reported but not predicted.

## 1. Specify

### Decisions on the round 2 proposals (autonomous defaults)

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 names the cause of C's priority drop. It is the only change made to C this round. |
| P2 | Adopt, with a change | The 10 new tickets (H01 to H10) are reported as a separate "hard slice". The main set stays the same as round 2, so each config can still be compared with its round 2 result. |
| P3 | Reject for now | Dropping D would remove the only cost configuration. D stays, and its one change is a retry cap of 1. That cap is the test of F6. I logged this in disagreements.md for the user to decide. |
| P4 | Adopt | n=3 cannot tell B's 0.02 miss apart from noise. Each cell gets 5 trials. Cells where the trials disagree can grow to 7 trials. |

### Round 3 requirement table (added to `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3-1 | In config C, `outage_status` is its own tool again. The other merged tools stay merged. | P1, r02 F4 | The harness saves C's tool list, and `outage_status` appears in it. C transcripts on outage tickets show a call to it. |
| R3-2 | Add 10 mixed billing and outage tickets, H01 to H10. Each has a gold category, gold priority, and an outage flag. Results for them are reported as a separate slice. | P2 | The ticket file has 10 entries that parse. The summary shows main set and hard slice results separately. |
| R3-3 | Config D allows at most 1 retry per ticket. Nothing else in D changes. | r02 F6, P3 rejected | No D transcript shows more than 1 retry. |
| R3-4 | 5 trials per cell. A split cell can get up to 2 extra trials, for a maximum of 7. | P4 | The completeness critic counts the trials in each cell. |
| R3-5 | A and B do not change. They are the controls. | Decision | The A and B config hashes match round 2. |
| R3-6 | The grader reads `label.priority` and never the draft reply. | r02 F5 | The grader selftest includes this case (see gate G1). |
| R3-7 | Trials cannot read gold labels, `grade.py`, or anything in `spe/predictions/` or `spe/prediction-log.md`. | Way rule | A peek scan reads every transcript. Any trial that read one of these files is voided. |
| R3-8 | Paid spend is capped at $30. A trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged. | Way rule | `skips.jsonl` and the spend log. |
| R3-9 | The round runs autonomously, with a local commit after each SPE step. | User's words, transcript r03 | `git log` shows the five commits and the `spe-r03` tag. Nothing is pushed. |

### `spe/spec/disagreements.md` entries (owner: the user)

- **r03-D1.** Drop config D (P3)? My default is to keep D and cap its retries at 1. If the user wants D dropped, round 4 drops it.
- **r03-D2.** Mixed tickets need a gold category rule. My default is that the gold category is the issue the customer asks us to act on first. The outage flag is recorded separately.
- **r03-D3.** The ±0.01 hit tolerance is kept so rounds stay comparable. Each row also gets a note saying whether the miss falls inside the 95% interval.

## 2. Predict

Each number starts from "same as last round". A number moves only for the reason given in its Why.

| # | Metric (grader check) | A | B | C | D |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Category accuracy, main set (`label.category == gold.category`) | 0.86 (same 0.86) | 0.86 (same 0.86) | **0.82** (same 0.80) | 0.74 (same 0.74) |
| 2 | Priority accuracy, main set (`label.priority == gold.priority`) | reported only | reported only | **0.76** (same 0.71) | reported only |
| 3 | Outage lookup call rate on tickets where `gold.outage == true` (code scan of transcript tool calls) | reported only | reported only | **0.90** (same 0.00) | reported only |
| 4 | Cost per ticket (API usage × price table, computed in code) | reported only | reported only | reported only | **$0.003** (same $0.004) |
| 5 | Category accuracy, hard slice H01 to H10 (`label.category == gold.category`) | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.65 | 0.55 |

**Why, one line per row:**
1. Only C changes. Its outage tickets get categorized correctly again because the separate lookup can confirm an outage. C stays below its round 1 score of 0.84 because the other tools are still merged. A, B, and D have no reason to move. For D, I assume retries mostly repeated the same answer. If D drops by more than 0.02, that assumption was wrong.
2. F4 says C's outage tickets got P3 because the status check was hidden. A separate tool brings the check back. I hold C 0.02 below its round 1 score of 0.78 because the other merges remain.
3. In round 2, C never called the check (F4). A separate tool with its own description should be called whenever a ticket names an outage. I predict 0.90 and not 1.00 because some tickets only hint at an outage.
4. F6 says retries doubled token use on long tickets. A cap of 1 retry removes most of that doubling. D cost $0.003 in round 1.
5. This is the first time the hard slice is measured, so there is no naive baseline. Mixed tickets have two plausible categories. I expect C and D to do worse than A and B. Row 5 does not count toward the 3-round stop streak.

Rows 1 to 4 are scored against the naive guess in the "Closer" column. Rows 1 to 4 hold 7 predicted cells.

## 3. Evaluate

### Gates before launch (any failure halts the round and I report)

- **G1 Grader selftest.** The oracle answers score 1.0. Empty output scores 0. Wrong labels score 0. One F5 case: the draft reply says "P1", `label.priority` says "P3", and gold is P3, so the trial must be scored correct. The reverse case must be scored wrong. All 10 hard-slice gold records must parse.
- **G2 Control regrade.** The current `grade.py` regrades the round 2 transcripts. It must reproduce A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, C priority 0.71, and D $0.004 exactly.
- **G3 Dry run.** Three cells get 1 trial each: C on T17 (the F4 cell, which must call `outage_status`), D on the longest ticket by token count (the F6 cell, which must show 1 retry or fewer), and A on H01 (to confirm that new tickets load and grade). The peek scan runs on these transcripts. Dry-run trials do not count toward results.
- **G4 Budget projection.** Projected spend must be $30 or less.

### Workflow `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`

- `const ROUND = 3` is the only place the round number appears. Paths and prompt text get `r03` from it through a pad helper.
- **Phase 1:** run gates G1 to G4.
- **Phase 2:** run trials for 4 configs × 50 tickets × 5 trials, which is 1,000 trials, with 8 running at a time. Each trial runs in a workdir that holds only the ticket and the config's tools. Each trial returns this schema: `{ticket_id, config, trial, label:{category, priority}, reply, tool_calls[], retries, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd}`. Code checks the schema. An invalid result is retried once, then recorded as an error.
- **Phase 3:** run the peek scan. It greps every transcript for `gold`, `grade.py`, `spe/predictions`, and `prediction-log`. Any trial that matches is voided and logged in `voids.jsonl`.
- **Phase 4:** add trials to split cells. A cell is split when its trials disagree on whether the answer is correct. Each split cell gets up to 2 extra trials. Extra trials are capped at 15% of the base trials.
- **Phase 5:** grade. All checks are code checks. No judge is needed this round.
- **Phase 6:** failure analysis. An Opus agent reads the failed transcripts and matches each one to F4, F6, or a proposed new F7 or higher.
- **Phase 7:** completeness critic, also on Opus. It checks that every predicted cell has a measured value, that the trial counts are right, that voids and skips are logged, and that C's tool list and D's retry counts were saved.
- Before each paid call, the script checks spend. If spend plus the estimated trial cost would pass $30, the trial is skipped and logged in `skips.jsonl`. If any base trial is skipped, the round halts.
- Outputs go to `spe/evals/results/r03/`: `trials.jsonl`, `grades.csv`, `voids.jsonl`, `skips.jsonl`, `summary.md`.

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "configs": ["A", "B", "C", "D"],
  "ticketSets": ["r02-main", "r03-hard"],
  "trialsPerCell": 5,
  "maxTrialsPerCell": 7,
  "maxExtraTrialsShare": 0.15,
  "budgetUsd": 30,
  "concurrency": 8,
  "dryRunCells": [["C", "T17"], ["D", "longest"], ["A", "H01"]]
}
```

### Cost estimate (not measured)

- D: 250 trials × $0.003 is about $0.75.
- A, B, and C have no measured cost. I assume about $0.012 per trial, so 750 trials cost about $9.00.
- Extra trials for split cells, up to 15%, cost about $1.50.
- The failure analysis and critic agents cost about $5 to $10.
- The total is about $16 to $21. The hard cap is $30.

### Halt and report if

A gate fails, the control regrade does not match, spend hits the cap, any trial reads gold or grader files, or a decision comes up that only the user can make.

1. Save the user's prompt verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`. Add the round 3 table to `spec.md` and update `disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r03 specify: adopt P1 P2 P4, keep D with retry cap`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` and has the author line "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, every number with its Why, and `same_as_last_round`. Mark `r03-draft.yaml` with `superseded_by: r03.yaml`. Commit `SPE r03 predict: C recovers outage priority, D cost back to $0.003`.
3. Write the C tool split, the D retry cap, the H01 to H10 tickets with gold labels, the F5 selftest case, and the workflow script. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the workflow. When it finishes, commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline taken from summary.md>`.

## 5. Close-out, when the completion notice arrives

- Add a round 3 section to `spe/prediction-log.md` with Verdict and Closer filled in. Under it, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the assumption that was wrong. I will say plainly if the naive guess won again.
- In `spe/failures.md`, record the outcome of the F4 and F6 fixes and add any new F entries. Original and regraded numbers go side by side.
- Add a "Proposed for round 4" table to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r03 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r03`.
- Stop check: the hit streak is 0 rounds, since round 2 hit 1 of 5 rows. The loop continues unless a halt condition fires.
